title: Physics-informed neural model predicts cervical cancer progression in retrospective cohorts
summary: Researchers at Vellore Institute of Technology report a physics-informed neural model for two-year progression-free survival prediction in cervical cancer, evaluated retrospectively in a 20,287-patient analytical cohort and two external Indian cohorts totaling 15,967 patients. The abstract reports internal time-dependent AUC 0.91 and external AUCs 0.87 and 0.86; the 2,663-patient 2023 temporal subset is included within the 3,043-patient held-out test set. Model-derived clusters with differing survival outcomes remain hypotheses requiring prospective validation. This source check covers the publisher abstract and publication metadata; it does not establish prospective patient benefit or causal biological mechanisms.
ai_technology: Physics-Informed Neural Surrogate Learning (PI-NSL), a neural model with a variational physics encoder, differentiable PDE solver and dynamic risk operator

evidence.tested: Retrospective internal held-out and historical external evaluation of progression-free survival prediction; reported latent patient-cluster survival differences.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical benefit and causal interpretation of clusters are not established. Full-paper methods and supplements were not assessed in this bounded independent review; broad geographic transfer is not established by the reported Indian cohorts.
evidence.ai_role: PI-NSL uses neural representations constrained by a mechanistic PDE system to estimate patient-specific parameters and predict progression-free survival; its latent representations support the reported patient clustering.

source_review.scope: Publisher article-in-press abstract, affiliations and publication metadata; full paper not assessed by independent reviewer
